## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

**Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 87** (*Itthālaṅkāra*, "Wearing jewelry") is an offense of expiation belonging to the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga of the Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule establishes that a Buddhist nun who wears ornaments or personal jewelry incurs a *pācittiya* offense requiring confession. An English translation of the rule has been completed by Bhikkhu Brahmali. Although several secondary Vinaya discussions cite a "Pācittiya 87," these references invariably concern the distinct rule on the permissible height of beds and couches found in the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga rather than this nun-specific regulation.
